title: Population recovery and a missing allele
instructions: Predict before running. Compare the size schedule with allele frequencies and exact counts. This synthetic experiment is one reproducible trial set, not a forecast for real populations.
prompts: Mark the first and last small generations and recovery. Predict the no-drift A frequency after recovery.
Compare N, A/a counts, frequency and H before, during and after the bottleneck. What do the constant-size trials show?
Follow a loss/fixation trial through recovery. Can an absent allele return? Explain the limits of these few paths.
adaptationNotes: Change severity, timing, duration or seed within this one example; hold other settings fixed. Initial/recovered N 3–500, small N 2 to initial N minus 1, 2–100 generations, recovery recorded, 1–4 trials per condition. This is reproduction/gene-copy resampling with replacement, not a cull or tracked survivors. H is one-locus gene diversity, not observed genotypes or genome diversity.
